Thunder shook the cauldron so hard the cauldron shook rings across the water, but everyone near me is still standing.
I checked hides, saddles, and dye vats after the lightning, then counted heads. No one should be alone after a sky like that.
Near the cauldron, the bell sounded small under that thunder. We stayed inside and kept the doors watched.
That thunder made everyone quiet. I checked the hides twice.
The sky can keep its lightning. I have hides to set right.
I checked dry hides and dye racks for sparks first, then checked faces for smoke and fear.
We passed water hand to hand and kept people away from the smoke. I checked the cauldron after.
The hides can wait. People come first.
We saved what we could reach around the cauldron, then stopped pretending things matter more than neighbors.
The smoke is thinning near the cauldron, but everyone is still sniffing the air like it might lie.
During a raid, the hides can soak another day; who makes it behind a door matters more.
The horns stopped, but my hands near the cauldron still expect another wave from the road.
We counted living neighbors before hides, saddles, and dye vats. That is the only count worth starting with.
Raiders came looking for easy emeralds. They found barred doors near the cauldron and a bell that would not stop ringing.
From the cauldron, I saw fear cross the square; then I saw courage get there first.
Night trouble tests the loose latch by the cauldron first. We are fixing those before sunset.
I stayed near the cauldron corner and listened for anyone calling from the dark.
Dawn gave the cauldron enough light to count wounds, missing blocks, and who made it home.
The dark tested everyone. Most of us passed by keeping stout boots between us and teeth.
We are safe enough near the cauldron, though every shadow is being inspected twice.
The wind threw sand through every crack. I am still cleaning sand out of the leather seams.
I checked hides, saddles, and dye vats, then checked who was coughing too hard to answer.

I am clearing stiff frost from the hides and watching for footprints that stop too soon.
